The first chord is given. • Study the piece of music on the following page. • Using the given rhythms, add melody and bass notes to complete the cadences and approach chords as follows: • (i) At A, an imperfect cadence with approach chord (I—ii—V) • (ii) At B, a plagal cadence with approach chord (vi—IV—I) • (iii) At C, an interrupted cadence with approach chord (IV—V—vi) • (iv) At D, a perfect cadence with approach chord (I—V—I)

schemeCrop.what: the “Given Chords” table: the chord symbol and Roman numeral for each chord of cadences A to D

grid.stem: Answer one question only in this section:
taskRequirements: Chord Progressions - General points
1. Same chord in adjacent boxes not accepted
2. Accidental and suffix, where relevant, must be fully correct for mark to be awarded
3. Chords must be part of a good progression
4. V – ii generally not accepted
5. ii – I generally not accepted
Good Progressions
1. Falling 3rd = generally better than rising 3rd
2. Rising 4ths
3. Cadence progressions anywhere
4. Primary triads
Bass Line
1. No doubling of major 3rd under chord symbol
2. Treatment of LN
3. Stepwise movement to and from inversions = good
4. Good finish
Consecutive 5ths, 8ves and exposed intervals are not considered here
If given rhythm is not used, consider under (i) Quality of Melody Line and/or (ii) Quality of Bass Line
If Melody Notes = 0, then Melody Quality Mark = 0
If Bass Notes = 0, then Bass Quality Mark = 0

criteria.label: 1 mark per correct note of chord
1 mark per correct melody note which is part of the given chord and which falls on the correct beat of the bar. The given rhythms must be used (1 x 12)
Up to 3 marks for quality of correct melody line at each cadence point, which fits well with the chord progression and correct bass notes (3 x 4)
1 mark per correct bass note of the given chord and which falls on the correct beat of the bar. The given rhythms must be used (1 x 12)
Up to 3 marks for quality of the correct bass line at each cadence point (3 x 4)

asks.notes: Section B: the scale and chord-bank work is MARKED at Ordinary Level ("Grid / Stave", 1 mark per correct note of chord, 1 x 12), so its bullets are part of the question text and its line is a counted criterion. The four cadence criteria are the scheme’s "Criteria for awarding marks at cadence points" lines, each 12 over the four cadences (the per-cadence table A-D prints the same lines at 1 x 3 and 3). The two "Up to 3 marks for quality ... (3 x 4)" lines carry no bands (no descriptors printed) and sit on 0-12. The Section B general points (scheme p11) are printed once for the section and are carried on all three questions’ task requirements. Q4’s (i)-(iv) name the cadences at A-D (as Q5 and Q6 do on the score); one ask, one total. "Bb" in the scale bullet is how the text layer prints B flat. The scheme’s "Given Chords" table (p13) is the scheme crop.
